title: A gym that pays MettleUp during its free trial loses its unused trial days, and a plan change carries the old paid days onto the new plan
what: When HQ confirms a payment, the paid month or year is counted from today or the current paid-until date; the free trial's end is ignored. A gym paying on day 3 of its trial loses the rest of the trial, while HQ's own confirm line says the paid time starts when the trial ends. A change of plan also moves all the days already paid onto the new plan: a gym with months of Starter left that pays one Pro month gets Pro for all of them, and a Pro gym that pays one Starter month drops to Starter at once for the rest of its paid Pro time. The later billing step that fixes both is not live.
expected: Paid time starts when the trial ends, and a plan change is priced or timed so neither MettleUp nor the gym loses paid days, with HQ's line showing the same date the server sets.
how_often: every gym that pays during its trial or switches plan
fix_line: Count paid time from the trial's end and handle a plan switch as its own case, as the next billing step already does, then make that step live

title: A gym that has paid but is still waiting for MettleUp to confirm is cut down to basic and then read-only like a gym that never paid
what: The gym's state comes only from its paid-until and trial dates. A payment the owner has sent and MettleUp has not yet confirmed counts for nothing, so once the plan limits are switched on, a gym whose confirmation waits more than 7 days on the one person who confirms loses new members and Pro extras, and after 37 days goes read-only.
expected: A gym with a payment waiting to be checked keeps everything on until MettleUp confirms or rejects it, and a payment left waiting raises an alarm that does not depend on one person looking.
how_often: whenever MettleUp is slow to confirm a payment, once plan limits are on
fix_line: Treat a waiting payment as paid for the state check, and remind MettleUp when one waits over a day

title: The nightly backup never copies member photos, workout report files or gym logos
what: The nightly copy holds every table but none of the stored files. If the database project were lost, every member photo taken at the desk and every workout report file would be gone for good; the restore guide says so, but nothing else copies them.
expected: Every file a gym or member relies on has a second copy somewhere else, or the gym is told plainly that photos are not backed up.
how_often: only if the database project is lost
fix_line: Add a weekly copy of stored files to a second store, or tell owners that photos have no backup

title: Every backup sits in the same Cloudflare account that runs the service, for 7 days, and only one person can open it
what: The nightly copy is kept only in Cloudflare, in the same account as the live service, and each copy is deleted after 7 days. Getting it back needs someone signed in to that account on a computer. If that one account is lost, locked or hacked, the live service and every backup go together, and a fault noticed after a week has no copy left from before it.
expected: At least one copy lives outside the main accounts, a second trusted person can reach it, and the way back in is written down.
how_often: only if that account is lost or a fault is found late
fix_line: Keep a weekly copy in a second, separate place and write down who else can reach it

title: If the Firebase key stops working, every phone pop-up is lost quietly and MettleUp is never told
what: Each pop-up job is marked as sent before it goes out. When the Firebase key is missing, wrong or refused, the sender only writes a line to the server log and the pop-ups of that batch are gone. Nothing in HQ shows that pop-ups have stopped; members only see the message later when the app checks by itself.
expected: A broken or refused pop-up key shows as a red line in HQ and sends MettleUp an alert the same day.
how_often: whenever the Firebase key breaks or expires
fix_line: Record each pop-up run's result where HQ's health check can see it and alert when runs fail

title: Help on sending messages never says there is a limit of 10 a day, no pop-up from the 3rd, and one offer a day
what: The server refuses an 11th message in a day, sends the 3rd and later messages with no phone pop-up, and allows one offer or event a day and three a week. The help article on sending messages and offers mentions none of these, so an owner who hits a limit has no help answer.
expected: The help article states the daily and weekly limits and the quiet rule in plain words.
how_often: every owner who sends many messages
fix_line: Add two lines on the limits to the message help article

title: A member's question to one trainer who never answers quietly closes after 14 days, and the owner never sees it
what: A question picked for one trainer is seen only by that trainer while they are still ticked. If that trainer ignores it, it stops being open after 14 days and the owner is never shown it, so the member's question reaches nobody.
expected: A question nobody has answered after a day or two is also shown to the owner, or the member is told and can ask someone else.
how_often: whenever a picked trainer does not reply
fix_line: Show questions unanswered for two days to the owner too

title: A gym that stops paying and never asks to leave keeps all its members' details on our server for ever
what: After the grace and basic days a gym goes read-only and stays that way with no end. Its members' names, phone numbers and payments are kept with no date for removal and no reminder to the owner or to MettleUp.
expected: A gym that stays read-only for a set time is warned, then removed or archived on a date the terms state.
how_often: every gym that leaves without asking
fix_line: Set and publish a time after which a read-only gym is warned and then deleted
